findings.title: Launched child inherits the parent's full environment, leaking secrets into a detached process
findings.description: `launch()` passes no `env` argument to `popen`, so `subprocess.Popen` inherits the entire parent environment. The docstring says "the inherited environment (Squadron's providers read credentials from it)", but this means every secret in Amoeba's environment (serve tokens, provider API keys, `AMOEBA_STORE_DIR`, and any other credential) is handed to a detached, long-lived child that outlives the tick. The project's own convention forbids ambient environment reads as a second source of truth, and the CLI test harness deliberately drops `TOKEN_ENV_VAR` "so a real one in the developer's shell must never reach a child" — but the production launch path has no such protection. The child should receive an explicitly constructed environment (e.g. the minimum needed for `PATH`/`HOME` plus the provider credentials Squadron actually requires), not the whole parent environment.

findings.title: The `sq` start-up probe can never pass against the real `sq` for a freshly minted id
findings.description: `probe_sq` mints a random run id and requires the answer to be `not_found` *for that exact id*. The `sq_stub` used by the tests was modified in this diff to emit exactly `{"run_id": "$3", "outcome": "not_found"}` and exit 5, i.e. the stub was made to satisfy the assertion rather than the assertion being derived from a real `sq` contract (`tests/detection_e2e_harness.py:99-112`). A real `sq runs wait <unknown-id>` may answer `not_found` without echoing the requested id, or may exit with a different code/shape; `poll_run` would then return a `PollFailure` ("printed an invalid document" or "exit code means X but the document says Y"), and `runner_tenant()` would raise `StartupFailedError` and the whole process would refuse to start. Nothing in the diff verifies this shape against a real Squadron; the only evidence is the stub that was written to match. Given "never use silent fallback values / fail explicitly", failing the entire start-up on an unverified assumption is a legitimate risk that needs confirmation against the real tool.

findings.title: A `sq run` child that exits 2 is treated as an upstream shape error and kills the whole process
findings.description: `ProjectTick._record_finished` converts any `LaunchFailed` with `failure is LaunchFailure.USAGE_ERROR` into an `UpstreamShapeError`, which `RunnerTenant._tick_project` deliberately re-raises so the process exits (exit code 15). The exit code 2 is hard-coded as "the child rejected its command line" (`src/amoeba/runner/observe.py:44`), but `sq run` can exit 2 for reasons that have nothing to do with the shape the Runner needs — a bad pipeline name, a missing provider, a malformed `-p` parameter value. In those cases the Runner kills the resident process for every project instead of blocking the one node. The distinction between "Squadron lacks `--run-id`" and "Squadron rejected this run's arguments" is not actually made; the message text is assumed.

findings.title: `PARAM_CHECKOUT` is stored but the checkout path is never validated, and it is journaled verbatim into the store
findings.description: The checkout path comes straight from the planner's `LaunchRun.checkout` and is written into the journal parameters as `str(action.checkout)` with no check that it is absolute, exists, or is inside the project tree — while `PARAM_CHECKOUT`'s own docstring says "the absolute path the launch runs in". `launch()` then passes it as `cwd=checkout` to `Popen`; a relative path would be resolved against the Amoeba process's working directory, and a path outside the project could run an arbitrary pipeline in an arbitrary directory. The project conventions require validating everything entering the system at the trust boundary; the planner is currently an internal seam but the value is also persisted in the journal and shown by `amoeba inspect`, so an unvalidated absolute path from any future planner (or a submission-driven planner in slice 124/125) becomes a command-execution primitive.

findings.title: The `_params_parameter` cast silently accepts a non-`Mapping` check that the store's JSON decode cannot satisfy
findings.description: `cast("Mapping[object, object]", raw)` is used to widen a `Mapping[str, object]` to `Mapping[object, object]` so that the non-`str` key/value checks can run. The cast is a static-only assertion; at runtime `raw` is whatever `json.loads` produced, and the store's `decode_mapping` already guarantees a `dict` with string keys — but the values are `object`, which is exactly why the check exists. The pattern works, but it silently defeats the type checker on the one boundary where malformed journal data would be dangerous: a value that is a `dict` or `list` (not a `str`) is correctly rejected, yet the `cast` means pyright cannot see the narrowing and the `Mapping` import in `launch.py` is used for two different notions of "mapping". A `dict[str, object]` narrowing (as `mapping_journal.decode_mapping` already produces) would remove the cast entirely.

findings.title: `RunnerTenant.tick` reports `wrote=False` for a tick that launched a child but launched nothing else
findings.description: The tick's return value is documented as "True only if something was written to a store or a command issued". `ProjectTick._launch` sets `self.wrote = True` when it journals the entry, so a launch does set it — but `self.wrote` is only read *after* `tick.run(budget)` returns, and `_launch` is reached through `_act`, which returns `TickResult.CUT_OFF` and makes `run()` return early. In the cut-off path the journal write has already happened and `wrote` is True, so this specific case is fine. The real gap is the opposite one: `RunnerTenant.tick` computes `wrote = wrote or project_wrote`, but `project_wrote` is `tick.wrote` evaluated as the *second element of the tuple returned by `_tick_project`* — and `_tick_project` returns `tick.run(budget), tick.wrote`, where `tick.wrote` is read *after* `run()` returns, so it is correct. This is fragile but not currently wrong; the concern is that the "wrote" signal is derived from a mutable attribute read at a distance rather than returned explicitly, which makes the contract in the docstring dependent on evaluation order.

findings.title: The Runner has no load test, despite touching subprocess, environment and concurrency paths
findings.description: The Python rules require at least one load test for any code on the simulation, network, concurrency or environment-layer paths, asserting latency/throughput/resource bounds. The Runner launches detached subprocesses, polls them, reaps them, and shares a `LaunchTracker` across ticks and projects, but `tests/load/` contains no Runner coverage (only `test_crash_loop.py` for the older journaling tenant). The unit tests are thorough, but nothing exercises many in-flight runs, many projects, or the tick-budget behaviour under load.

findings.title: `build_argv` validates parameter keys and values but not the pipeline name or run id
findings.description: `build_argv` carefully rejects `,` and `=` in parameter keys and `,` in values, but the `pipeline` and `run_id` arguments are inserted into the argv verbatim with no validation. `mint_run_id` produces a conforming id and the pattern exists (`SQUADRON_RUN_ID_PATTERN`) but is never applied at runtime — the docstring says "The pattern is checked by tests, not at runtime". A pipeline name beginning with `-` would be parsed by `sq` as a flag. This is currently only reachable from a planner, but the same trust-boundary concern as the checkout path applies.

findings.title: `escalate()` blocks a node without checking that the node belongs to the project in context
findings.description: `escalate` looks up the node by id from `NodeContext` and, if it exists, has no in-flight run and is not `DONE`, blocks it — without verifying `node.project_id == project_id`. `NodeContext` is set from `entry.node_id` and `action.node_id`, which come from the project's own store, so in practice the ids are consistent; but the store's `block()` writes a blocked state whose `project_id` comes from the node, so a mismatch would silently write to another project's node. A cheap `node.project_id == project_id` assertion would make the invariant explicit.
